newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union hopeful of Ford Canada deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada union hopeful of Ford Canada deal.

text.p: The Canadian Auto Workers union voiced optimism on Monday that a contract deal with Ford Motor Co. of Canada Ltd. could soon be within reach after the company said it would present its economic offer later on Monday.

CAW President Buzz Hargrove said the union could reach a tentative agreement as soon as Monday night if the economic package mirrors the pattern deal forged recently with the Canadian units of Chrysler Corp. and General Motors Corp.

"If we can resolve all of the issues to our satisfaction and the only thing is language that we will have to work out, we will announce a tentative agreement subject to the language reflecting the agreement in principle we have," said Hargrove.
The CAW, which represents about 11,700 Ford workers, has set a strike deadline of 7 P.M. EST on Wednesday if a deal cannot be reached.
"There will be an offer made sometime this evening," said Ford spokesman Jim Hartford, who suggested the offer would come at about 7 P.M. EST on Monday.
Hartford declined to say whether the package would mirror the pattern agreement.
"I think we'll have to wait until (Ford's chief negotiator Donald) McKenzie gets here this evening to find that out," said Hartford.

The framework deal with Chrysler and GM offered the union protection from outsourcing, or contracting out jobs, ensured minimum health and safety and employment standards and gave workers improved benefits and a 10.2 percent wage and cost of living increase over three years.
Ford and the CAW were working to settle local issues, including working conditions at Ford's Oakville, Ontario, truck and van assembly plant.
While not ruling out an early settlement, a source close to the union said talks would likely go down to the wire simply because labour pacts are rarely settled two days before a strike deadline.
"I haven't seen many examples of it going early," said the source.
But Hargrove said the early presentation of Ford's economic package left him optimistic a deal could be reached without a work stoppage.

"I'm assuming and hopeful and expecting that (McKenzie) will meet the pattern without much of a fight here," said Hargrove. "When he called us in the middle of our caucus to say that he's going to table a comprehensive economic proposal at seven (o'clock) tonight, that's reason for optimism."

In October, talks between the union and GM Canada broke down after the company presented its economic offer just hours before the strike deadline. The ensuing 20-day strike by 26,000 GM workers disrupted production across North America.
Ford Canada is a wholly owned unit of Ford Motor Co.
